In 2020 Rae formed HOORAE, a multi-faceted media company that develops content across mediums in an effort to continue to break boundaries in storytelling and representation. Arlan Hamilton, founder at Backstage Capital, is a serial entrepreneur, author, and prolific speaker. She founded Backstage Capital in 2015 to invest in founders who are people of color, women and/or LGBTQ. Since its founding, Backstage has raised $30 million and invested in more than 200 startups led by underestimated founders.
Arlan published her debut book, “It’s About Damn Time,” in 2020, detailing her journey from homelessness to venture capital trailblazer. Arlan was the first non-celebrity Black woman to grace the cover of Fast Company magazine. Her latest book, ""Your First Million: Why You Don't Have To Be Born Into A Legacy Of Wealth To Leave One Behind"", shows how anyone can tap into new tools, platforms, and funding sources to get their million-dollar idea off the ground.

Arlan is a big proponent of paying it forward and supporting other underestimated people in the tech industry and beyond. She and her mother, Mrs. Earline Butler-Sims, have established scholarship programs for Black students at Oxford University, HBCU Dillard University, and Harvard Law, as well as establishing scholarships for Black pilots and inventors.

Join Dr. Priscilla Chan, co-founder and co-CEO of the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) in conversation with Bloomberg Originals host, Emily Chang, as they explore how advances in generative AI are shaping the future of medicine. She will discuss CZI’s vision to build AI-powered “virtual cells” – digital models that can predict human cell behavior. To support this vision, CZI is building one of the largest AI computing clusters for nonprofit life science research to enable AI for biomedicine at scale. These advancements could lead to faster, more efficient medical breakthroughs, real-time health monitoring, and advanced treatments.

Building virtual cells comes with significant challenges. Scientists face knowledge gaps in understanding the complex workings of the 37 trillion cells in the human body, such as the exact components of cells and their interactions in health and disease. Cells are dynamic and function on multiple scales and processes, which require specialized models — like models trained on data from sequencing and images — that are difficult to integrate into a unified virtual cell. Developing accurate models also depends on gathering vast amounts of high-quality data across various modalities and species.

Priscilla will highlight the importance of cross-disciplinary collaboration and open science in overcoming these scientific and technological hurdles as we work toward creating AI systems capable of accurately simulating cellular functions. Ultimately, this progress will be key to reaching CZI’s mission to cure, prevent, or manage all diseases by the end of this century.

Join IBM Chairman & CEO Arvind Krishna for a discussion on how business and society can benefit from the convergence of these next frontiers in technology.

xWL4Y23gYRk.title: AI’s Agentic Near Future
xWL4Y23gYRk.label: SXSW 2025 keynotes & featured
xWL4Y23gYRk.description:
Portuguese and Spanish language translations for SXSW 2025 Keynotes and Featured Sessions presented by Itaú.  

Prompting AIs is great, but has an AI prompted YOU yet? The Agentic Era is dawning, and with the active participation of AI agents business is about to get weirder and wildly more productive. Learn how we’re already prompting AIs with our behavior and how spatial computing agents will connect businesses with the many kinds of ecosystems they inhabit, leading to automatically evolving enterprises that adapt in real-time. We’ll explore how humans and technology are actively co-creating reality, plus practical ways AI agents already unlock exponential productivity and sustainable business growth.

By skillfully connecting the possible with the practical, Neil Redding is a Near Futurist and Innovation Architect with 30+ years of experience unlocking the transformative power of emerging technologies. A sought-after keynote speaker at SXSW, Dubai Future Forum, and AWE, and at corporate events for Meta, Microsoft, and more, Neil inspires audiences with the reality-shifting capabilities of AI and spatial computing for activating pragmatic interpersonal and business value. Through his boutique consultancy Redding Futures and previous roles, Neil has worked with world-class brands including Visa, Nike, Apple, and Verizon to distill these continually emerging possibilities, applying ecosystem-centered design to unlock sustainable growth, resilience, and transformative business opportunity.

y9WPp-g0LBs.title: Weirding the Digital: An Invocation with Douglas Rushkoff
y9WPp-g0LBs.label: SXSW 2025 keynotes & featured
y9WPp-g0LBs.description:
Portuguese and Spanish language translations for SXSW 2025 Keynotes and Featured Sessions presented by Itaú

The net began as a haven for the counterculture and a catalyst for strange new possibilities, yet it quickly surrendered to the needs of the market for predictability and profits. Digital technologies promote utilitarian ends instead of creative ones, and artificial intelligence favors the probable over the possible. It's time to talk ourselves down off this bad trip and - in the spirit of the OG SXSW - to fold the weirdest fringes back to the center of our digital society. This session will initiate the next interactive age. Convened by Douglas Rushkoff, celebrating the new 15th anniversary edition of his classic text, Program or Be Programmed.
